page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-16 is a compute-optimized virtual machine provisioned on x86_64 architecture using AMD EPYC 7B13 processors. It features 16 virtual CPUs backed by 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core using dedicated CPU allocation. The system configuration includes 16 GB of system RAM, providing a memory allocation ratio of 1.0 GB per vCPU. Cache infrastructure consists of 32 KB L1 data cache per core, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It lacks attached local storage and discrete GPUs, relying on remote network storage for persistence.

Instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, VAES, SHA_NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA, supporting accelerated cryptographic operations and vector computations. Benchmark evaluations place single-core CPU stress-ng performance in the top 25% percentile, while multi-core CPU testing falls within the middle 50% percentile with a score of 21558.27. Memory bandwidth tests yield uncached read speeds of 75.4 GB/sec and uncached write speeds of 40.36 GB/sec. Application benchmarks reflect average tier results, including a PassMark CPU score of 22027.2, static web serving throughput of 15.62 GB/sec, and Redis SET throughput of 16.05 million operations per second. Small LLM inference tests using a 135M model achieve 904.0 prompt tokens/sec and 242.73 generation tokens/sec.

The compute-heavy ratio of 16 vCPUs to 16 GB memory makes this instance cost-effective for CPU-bound workloads that do not require extensive memory capacity. However, the low RAM-to-vCPU ratio presents a tradeoff for memory-intensive applications or large in-memory databases. The instance is suited for batch processing, compilation tasks, lightweight web serving, cryptographic execution, and microservices where CPU throughput is prioritized over memory footprint.
